name: South Kaibab Trail to Skeleton Point
why: Down an open ridge into the canyon, past Ooh Aah Point and Cedar Ridge, to the first view of the Colorado River.
book: No permit for a day hike. No parking at the trailhead: take the free Kaibab Rim (orange) shuttle. Going to the river and back in one day is strongly advised against by the park.
water: No water on the trail: carry 3-4 litres. Fill up at the trailhead.
dangers: The climb out takes twice as long as the way down.
Heat over 38°C in summer: no shade at all.
Mule trains have the right of way.
turnaround: Turn at Skeleton Point; in summer hike before 10:00 or after 16:00.

points.name: South Kaibab trailhead
points.note: Yaki Point road, reached by shuttle only.

points.name: Ooh Aah Point
points.note: The first wide view east along the canyon.

points.name: Cedar Ridge
points.note: A flat ridge with toilets, a good place to turn for a short walk.

points.name: Skeleton Point
points.note: The edge of the Redwall: first sight of the Colorado River far below.
